How to use the plain-text tool

  1. Paste into the input box using your device’s normal Paste command.
  2. Choose Make plain text and review the result.
  3. Choose Copy result, then paste into your destination.

If clipboard access is unavailable, the result is selected so you can copy manually. Undo restores the previous input and result after a conversion, sample or clear action.

What “plain text” means here

A text box accepts characters rather than rich formatting, so copying its result removes source fonts, colors, embedded images and rich hyperlink markup. Ordinary words, emoji, tabs and line breaks are preserved.

Pasting literal HTML code does not render it or remove its tags. It remains text. If you want to join wrapped PDF lines as well, use the line-break remover.

Your text is not our data

Conversion runs locally in the browser. Input and undo state live in memory only: no local storage, server upload, URL parameters or text analytics. Reloading or leaving the page loses the input. Copy only runs when you press the copy button; the tool never reads the clipboard.

The hosting service still handles normal page requests as described in the privacy notice. Browser extensions and your own device can have their own access rules.

Need this in your Windows workflow?

Clipora’s native app can save your copied text and paste a selected clip without rich formatting using Alt + Enter. The browser tool is for a one-off conversion; the app is for a reusable library.

Read the Windows plain-paste guide.
